on_device.stays_on_the_device: Everything in these files stays on the device, until the game is uninstalled or the player removes it.

network.every_request: Sent to this server over HTTPS, and shows the server the device's IP address.
network.ip_addresses: The server's proxy and request log see the IP address of every request, and its rate-limit notes can hold it. The game neither reads nor sends it as data, and it is not used to work out a location. How long each is kept is stated by the server's own privacy policy.
network.outside_services: The game has no analytics, crash-reporting, advertising or attribution services.

requests.when: The first time this device creates or joins a group: the game asks the server for an anonymous token.
At launch and when the groups' screen opens, once this device has a token.
When the player creates a group.

body.join_code: the code of the group to join, which the player taps in

requests.when: When the player joins a group with a code.
When the player opens a group.
When the player opens a group, and whenever a group's title looks different from when it was last read.
When the player holds Leave on a group.
When the player holds the delete control (see deletion).

body.score: the score of a game that counts: played by a group member, with dots sized to the screen, not the tutorial's

requests.when: After a game that counts, or at the next contact if it could not be sent then, while the player is in a group.

query.started_on: the date this device first played

requests.when: When the game is online, to learn which themes are available; for every player, Free too, with no token.

ruby_gems.lota: the game engine: draws, plays sound, reads input

sensors.accelerometer: The accelerometer is read only while the game-over pile is on screen, to tilt the dots. It is neither stored nor sent.

sharing.how: Only when the player chooses "Share my score". On a phone the text goes to the system's own share sheet, and elsewhere to a preview with a copy button. The game does not send it anywhere itself.

apple.ip_addresses: The server's proxy and request log see the IP address of every request, and its rate-limit notes can hold it. The game neither reads nor sends it as data, and it is not used to work out a location. How long each is kept is stated by the server's own privacy policy. Apple's list has no IP-address category, so it is not among the data types; if the maintainer or Apple's review reads "Device ID" as covering it, add that, linked and for App Functionality.

google.ip_addresses: The server's proxy and request log see the IP address of every request, and its rate-limit notes can hold it. The game neither reads nor sends it as data, and it is not used to work out a location. How long each is kept is stated by the server's own privacy policy. The maintainer decides whether to list it under Device or other IDs.

declared_but_not_enforced: What Apple and Google do with a purchase: it goes straight from the device to their store, in the iOS and Android hosts, and this game's server never sees it.
How the iOS and Android hosts, and the operating system's share sheet, behave beyond what their source shows: no test here runs them.
What Lota, LÖVE, SDL and Fledge's runtime do inside the app: audited by hand for their required-reason APIs, not by a test.

Permissions a library's own manifest adds when Android merges it in: ANDROID_MERGED records what billing 9.1.0's manifest says, and its transitive libraries are unchecked. Read the merged manifest of a release build.
What the server does with what it receives: its own privacy policy states that, and this repository cannot check it.
That a store's label definitions still fit these answers: Apple and Google change them, so re-read them when entering.
